# Research notes: Trump net approval in the RCP Average on Oct 15, 2026 (compiled Oct 6, 2026)

## 1. What the resolution source shows (it could not be read directly)
- **RCP page was blocked.** realclearpolling.com and realclearpolitics.com both returned HTTP 403 to all three researchers, and archive.org snapshots could not be fetched. Nobody has quoted the RCP Average row from RCP itself, so every RCP figure below is secondhand.
- **Oct 1, 2026:** RCP Average 38.2% approve, 60.3% disapprove, spread −22.1. Source: Wikipedia's table. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opinion_polling_on_the_second_Trump_presidency
  - This is exactly the example in the resolution criteria, so the question was probably written around Oct 1.
  - **Uncertain:** another table further down the same Wikipedia page shows 40.8/57.6 for Oct 1. That table may be out of date.
- **Oct 3, 2026:** 38.2/60.2, spread −22.0. **Uncertain:** this comes only from a search-engine summary; no article was found.
- **Sept 26–28, 2026:** RCP 38.7/59.9, spread −21.2. FITSNews (Sept 29) called it Trump's widest gap of either term, beating −21.1 on Dec 13, 2017. https://www.fitsnews.com/2026/09/29/donald-trump-peak-disapproval/
- **September 2026, record low:** a snippet from an RCP analysis piece says the spread reached −21.1, tying the first-term low, then "improved only marginally" to −20.9 (38.8/59.7). The article itself was blocked. https://www.realclearpolling.com/stories/analysis/trump-approval-rating-at-lowest-point-of-either-term
- **Sept 23, 2026:** a snippet gives 38.8/56.9 (−18.1). It conflicts with the other figures, so treat it as low confidence.
- **Kalshi's daily market on the RCP approve %** was around 38.7–38.9 in a search snippet. That snippet is unverified, and no volume could be obtained.
- **Resolution distance:** 9 days remain from Oct 6. As of about Oct 1–3, the spread was about −22.0 to −22.1, the lowest RCP spread of either term.

## 2. Recent news and the status quo
**Other polling averages**
- **Silver Bulletin, Oct 5:** net −21.9, recovering from an all-time low of −23.5 over Oct 3–4. Its issue ratings are all at all-time lows: inflation −48.5, economy −33.2, trade −29.0. https://www.natesilver.net/p/trump-approval-ratings-nate-silver-bulletin
- **Ballotpedia, end of September:** its own 30-day average (not RCP) was 39/60. Its second-term low was 38% on Sept 29, and September was the lowest month of the term. https://news.ballotpedia.org/2026/10/01/trump-saw-lowest-average-approval-rating-of-his-second-term-in-september/
- **Gallup** ended its presidential approval series in February 2026, so it no longer feeds into the averages. https://www.axios.com/2026/02/11/gallup-ends-presidential-approval-rating

  - https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2026-10-05/trump-approval-at-record-low-hispanic-voters-sour-on-republicans-reuters-ipsos-poll-finds
  - https://www.wfsb.com/2026/09/29/new-quinnipiac-poll-shows-low-approval-trumps-job-performance/

**What's driving it**
- **Iran war:** it began in late February 2026. US strikes resumed in mid-July after a ceasefire collapsed.
  - Trump rejected Iran's ceasefire proposal on Sept 26–29.
  - On Oct 2–3 he said the war would end "probably right after the midterms."
  - Sources conflict on whether the Strait of Hormuz is still closed.
- **Gas prices:** $4.37/gal on average, per Slate (Oct 5). https://slate.com/news-and-politics/2026/10/gas-prices-trump-midterms-iran-war-hormuz.html
- **Tariffs:** the Supreme Court struck down his main tariff authority.
- **Jobs:** the September report (released Oct 2) showed +29K jobs and 4.2% unemployment.
- **Shutdown:** per uspollingdata, a stopgap funds the government through Dec 11. **Unverified.** The base-rates researcher described a "shutdown fight," so this conflicts.

**Scheduled events, Oct 6–15**
- **Iran:** ceasefire and talks news is ongoing.
- **Oct 14:** September CPI release.
- **Senate debates:** Oct 7 and 13 (Iowa), Oct 8 (Michigan, Georgia), Oct 11 (South Carolina).
- **New polls:** the usual weekly releases (Reuters/Ipsos, Economist/YouGov and others).
- **Midterms:** Nov 3, 2026, after the resolution date.

**Prediction markets**
- **Polymarket (seen Oct 6, 2026).** These markets reportedly resolve on Silver Bulletin, not RCP.
  - "How low will Trump's approval go in 2026?" ($158K volume, $23K liquidity): ≤37% at 94–97¢, ≤36% at 79¢, ≤35% at 28¢, ≤34% at 17¢.
  - "Trump approval on Oct 9" ($2.8K volume, thin): leading bin 37.5–37.9% at 33¢.
- **Kalshi:** the page returned errors, so there are no verified prices or volumes. Snippets show below 36% this year at about 67–72% and below 35% at about 38%.

## 3. Base rates
- **Trajectory of the RCP net:**
  - About +7.8 in late January 2025.
  - Negative since late March 2025.
  - About −10 at the end of 2025.
  - Gradual slide through 2026, with the low-to-mid −20s reached in Sept–Oct.
  - The monthly 2026 RCP values are uncertain.
- **First term for comparison:** RCP yearly nets were −13.5 (2017), −10.7 (2018), −9.9 (2019) and −8.7 (2020). The low was about −20/−21 in December 2017, which recovered to about −13 within 6–8 weeks. https://orig.realclearpolitics.com/epolls/other/president_trump_job_approval-6179.html
- **Short-term volatility.** This is the researcher's estimate from memory, medium-low confidence; no daily data could be obtained.
  - Trump's RCP net usually moves less than 1.5 points over 10 days.
  - Moves above 2 points happen in perhaps 10–20% of 10-day windows.
  - Moves above 3 points happen in about 5% or fewer, usually tied to a shock.
  - Over a month, 1–3 points is typical.
- **Last month before a midterm.** From memory, medium confidence.
  - 2018: Trump improved by about 2–4 points into Election Day.
  - 2022: Biden was flat, within about 1–2 points.
  - 2010: Obama was flat.
  - Typical movement is 2 points or less, with no consistent direction.

## Main uncertainties
- **No direct reading of the RCP page.** The −22.0/−22.1 figures for Oct 1–3 come from Wikipedia and a search snippet.
- **Conflicting secondary RCP figures:** 40.8/57.6 and 38.8/56.9.
- **Unknown poll mix:** which polls are currently in the RCP window can't be confirmed, so a single poll entering or leaving could shift it by about 1 point.

criterios: This question resolves to the "Spread" value shown in the "RCP Average" row of the RealClearPolitics (RealClearPolling) "President Trump Job Approval" page at https://www.realclearpolling.com/polls/approval/donald-trump/approval-rating as of the end of October 15, 2026 (US Eastern Time), computed as the Approve percentage minus the Disapprove percentage. For example, an RCP Average of 38.2% approve and 60.3% disapprove resolves as -22.1. Report the signed value, including the negative sign if approval is below disapproval.

If the page is permanently unavailable with no archived snapshot, the question is annulled.

(a) **Time left:** The outcome is known at the end of October 15, 2026, nine days from now.

(b) **If nothing changed:** The spread stays about where it was on October 1–3, around −22.0 to −22.1. This figure comes secondhand from Wikipedia and a search snippet, since the RCP page itself could not be read.

(c) **If the trend continued:** The slide through September and early October would continue slowly. That gives about −22.5 to −23.5. Two things push that way: the Reuters/Ipsos poll at −33 is entering the average, and the issue ratings are at record lows. Silver Bulletin, however, has bounced from −23.5 back to −21.9, which suggests the decline may be leveling off.

(d) **Experts and markets:**
- Silver Bulletin stands at −21.9.
- Polymarket's ladder implies approval may drift slightly lower, into the 36–37% range by Silver Bulletin's measure. That points to a modest further decline, not a collapse.
- Historically, the month before a midterm is roughly flat, sometimes improving slightly for the president.
- The RCP average moves slowly and typically shifts less than 1.5 points over ten days.

(e) **Low scenario:**
- The Iran war escalates or gas prices spike.
- The October 14 CPI report is bad.
- Several harsh polls (AP-NORC, CNN, Quinnipiac) enter the window while friendlier polls (Harvard-Harris, Rasmussen) drop out.
- Together these push the spread to −25 or worse.

(f) **High scenario:**
- A ceasefire or reopening of the Strait of Hormuz brings gas prices down.
- Midterm partisan consolidation lifts Republican identifiers back toward Trump.
- Friendly pollsters dominate the window.
- Together these pull the spread back to about −19 or −20.

I centre the forecast slightly below the current level, at about −22.1, with a moderately wide interval to allow for unknowns.
